# Lab 1 Assignment

## Prepare Your Repository

::: {.callout-caution}
This assignment workflow is for students enrolled in the NCKU course. Follow
the newest course announcement if it conflicts with an older copy of this
document.
:::

Open the Lab 1 assignment link provided by the teaching staff and accept the
assignment in **Classroom50**. Classroom50 creates an individual GitHub
repository from the 2026 Lab 1 template.

Clone that repository inside the prepared course development environment:

```{.shell}
git clone <link_to_your_own_repo>
cd <your_repository>
git submodule update --init --recursive
pre-commit install
```

::: {.callout-note}
The `riscv-tests` directory is a Git submodule. If it is empty, or if test
programs are missing, run the submodule command above before building.
:::

## What You Need to Implement

There are two files you are expected to modify for Lab 1:

1. `src/core.c` --- implement the missing behavior in `Core_decode()` and
   `Core_execute()`.
2. `report.md` --- complete the assignment report.

For the program implementation itself, the primary file you should modify is
`src/core.c`. Your ISS must support the 37 required RV32I instructions
described in the previous chapters.

::: {.callout-warning}
Do not modify the build system, public tests, the `riscv-tests` submodule, or
the Classroom50 grading workflow unless the teaching staff explicitly asks
you to do so. The official grader evaluates your `src/core.c` inside a clean,
authoritative framework; modifying local infrastructure cannot change the
official score.
:::

Your implementation must:

- classify every required encoding in `Core_decode()`;
- apply the corresponding state transition in `Core_execute()`;
- preserve `x0` as zero;
- handle immediate values and signedness correctly;
- access memory through the provided MemoryMap interface; and
- update the PC correctly for sequential and control-flow instructions.

## Build and Run Tests

First build the RISC-V test programs from the repository root:

```{.shell}
make -C riscv-tests/isa -j
```

Configure and build the ISS in a separate build directory:

```{.shell}
cmake -S . -B build
cmake --build build --parallel
```

Run all 37 registered CTest cases:

```{.shell}
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
```

To list the registered tests without running them:

```{.shell}
ctest --test-dir build -N
```

To run one instruction, such as ADD:

```{.shell}
ctest --test-dir build -R '^OP_add$' --output-on-failure
```

To run one opcode group, such as OP-IMM:

```{.shell}
ctest --test-dir build -R '^OPIMM_' --output-on-failure
```

::: {.callout-note}
The values passed to `-R` are [regular
expressions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regular_expression). You can use
[regex101](https://regex101.com/) to experiment with a pattern.
:::

The public CTest cases provide local feedback. During formal grading,
Classroom50 places the submitted `src/core.c` into a clean framework, builds
it, and runs one isolated case for each of the 37 required instructions. The
independent cases prevent one broken support instruction from automatically
causing unrelated instruction cases to fail.

## Grading

The 100-point base score consists of the 80-point program and the 20-point
report. The current `report.md` also contains an optional 2-point bonus
question.

| Part | Score |
| --- | ---: |
| ISS compilation | 10 pts |
| 37 instruction cases | 70 pts |
| Assignment report | 20 pts |
| Optional bonus report question | +2 pts |

The 70 instruction points are divided into nine opcode groups:

| Group | Cases | Score |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| OP | 10 | 15 pts |
| OP-IMM | 9 | 15 pts |
| LOAD | 5 | 8 pts |
| STORE | 3 | 8 pts |
| BRANCH | 6 | 8 pts |
| JAL | 1 | 4 pts |
| JALR | 1 | 4 pts |
| LUI | 1 | 4 pts |
| AUIPC | 1 | 4 pts |

Compilation is all-or-nothing: a successful build earns 10 points. If the
submission does not compile, Compilation receives 0 points, the instruction
groups are marked as skipped, and the Program score is 0/80.

Within each opcode group, points are proportional to the number of passing
cases and rounded to the nearest integer, with an exact half rounded up:

```text
group score = round-half-up(group maximum × passed cases / total cases)
```

For example, passing 9 of the 10 OP cases gives:

```text
15 × 9 / 10 = 13.5 → 14 points
```

::: {.callout-important}
Classroom50 reports only the **Program score out of 80**. The teaching staff
grades `report.md` out of 20 and adds the optional 2-point bonus separately.
:::

## Submission through Classroom50

The 2026 Lab 1 assignment uses **every push to the default branch** as a
submission. You do not need to create a submission tag or upload a ZIP file.

Before pushing:

1. remove temporary debug output;
2. complete `report.md` in place;
3. review the files changed by `git diff` and `git status`;
4. commit the intended `src/core.c` and `report.md`; and
5. push the commit to the default branch of your Classroom50 repository.

```{.shell}
git status
git add src/core.c report.md
git commit -m "Complete Lab 1"
git push
```

Each push starts the autograder. GitHub shows the result as a commit status,
and Classroom50 publishes a submission Release containing the detailed
program result. A failed test status does not mean that the grading
infrastructure crashed; open the result to see the score and failed groups.

Only committed and pushed work is submitted. The teaching staff uses the
latest accepted submission before the announced deadline. Check Classroom50
and the course announcement for the actual deadline.

## Final Submission Checklist

- [ ] I implemented all 37 required RV32I instructions.
- [ ] `Core_decode()` classifies every required encoding.
- [ ] `Core_execute()` produces the required state changes.
- [ ] `x0` remains zero and control-flow instructions update the PC correctly.
- [ ] The project builds without warnings or errors.
- [ ] All 37 local CTest cases pass.
- [ ] I did not modify tests, CMake files, the submodule, or grading workflow.
- [ ] Temporary traces and debug output are removed.
- [ ] `report.md` contains my name, student ID, and required answers.
- [ ] I reviewed and committed the intended changes.
- [ ] I pushed the final commit before the deadline.
- [ ] I checked the Classroom50 result for the pushed commit.
